excerpt: பொங்கிடும் மங்களம் தந்தருள்வாய் அம்பிகே ஶ்ரீ லலிதே

sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
பொங்கிடும் மங்களம் தந்தருள்வாய் அம்பிகே ஶ்ரீலலிதே
கிங்கிணி ஓசையுடனே எங்கும் நிறைந்த ஈஸ்வரியே வந்தருள்வாய்
sections.translit:
pongidum mangaLam thandharuLvAy ambikE srIlalithE
kingkiNi OsaiyudanE engum niRaindha IswariyE vandharuLvAy
sections.en: Goddess Sri Lalitha, please bless us with prosperity. Oh, omnipresent goddess, please rush to us with the melodic sound of your swaying anklet and bestow your compassion.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
வானினும் உயர்ந்தே நின்றிட அறிவும் திறனும்
வீணா கானமும் பல்கலையும் நல்கிடுவாய் நாமகளே
எழிலே உருவான அலைமகளே கோமளவல்லியே
நெல்லிக்கனி ஒன்றினுக்கீடாய் பொன் மழை பொழிந்தாற் போல்
sections.translit:
vAninum uyarndhE nindRida aRivum thiRanum
vINA gAnamum palkalaiyum nalgiduvAy nAmagaLE
ezhilE uruvAna alaimagaLE kOmaLavalliyE
nellikkani ondRinukkIdAy pon mazhai pozhindhAR pOl
sections.en: Goddess of knowledge, please enable us to stand as tall as the sky with intellect, skills, musical knowledge of the veena (string instrument), and mastery of several arts. Oh, beautiful goddess Komalavalli, who sprung from the ocean’s waves, please bless us with prosperity – just as you once showered gold, overwhelmed by the offer of a tiny gooseberry fruit by a poor devotee.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
கனலினை அணைத்திட சரவணமாய் நின்ற சியாமளே
மூன்றுருவும் ஒருங்கிணைந்தே சர்வ சக்தி ரூபமாய்
நின்றே மகிஷனை மாய்த்தும் காலிடைக் கொண்ட காருண்ய ஜோதியே
பதகமலம் பிடித்தே பாரெலாம் உய்ந்திட திடசித்தியுடனே
sections.translit:
kanalinai aNaitthida saravaNamAy nindRa syAmaLE
mUndRuruvum orungiNaindhE sarva sakthi rUpamAy
nindRE magishanai mAytthum kAlidaik koNda kAruNya jOthiyE
padhakamalam piditthE pArelAm uyndhida dhidasiddhiyudanE
sections.en: Oh, Goddess of energy & tranquility, you took the form of the Saravana pond to hug the fire that emanated from the third eye of Lord Siva, causing the birth of Muruga. You stood combining the persona of all three divine forms together with infinite strength. You are the shining source of compassion, keeping even the evil Mahishasura under your divine feet after killing his evil mind. Bless all the people of the world, who have surrendered under your lotus feet, with willpower & eternal auspiciousness.

notes: Ambal Sri Lalitha is considered a combination of the three female goddesses: Saraswathi, Parvathi, and Lakshmi, per Hindu mythology, and the poet has espoused this idea in this song. The charanam of this song includes the story of Parvathi absorbing Lord Siva’s sparks in the form of a mystical body of water called the Saravana pond. The sparks became six babies, which she hugged all together and transformed them into one form with six faces and twelve hands named Arumuga. Six babies transformed into Arumuga Parvathi’s body is the Saravana pond that accepted Siva’s six sparks. Parasakthi is the only one that could accept that kind of heat. Agni, Vayu, and the Ganges that carried the sparks struggled hard and then dropped and deposited them in the divine pond. This idea is derived from Mahaperiyava’s discussions. For details see: தெய்வத்தின் குரல், ஜகத்குரு ஶ்ரீகாஞ்சி காமகோடி பீடாதீச்வர ஶ்ரீசந்திரசேகரேந்திர சரஸ்வதி சங்கராசாரிய ஸ்வாமிகளின்அருள்வாக்குகள், முதற் பகுதி, வானதி பதிப்பகம், 13 தீனதயாளு தெரு, தி.நகர், சென்னை – 17, ஒன்பதாம் பதிப்பு டிசம்பர்1992, பக்கங்கள் 672-673. The charanam also has another legend associated with Goddess Lakshmi showering gold onto a poor lady who could only offer a gooseberry to Adisankara when he went to her home for alms. The young sanyasi burst out into Kanakadhara stotram, singing the praise of Lakshmi and pleading with the goddess to help the poor lady.
